property_summary: For any positive funding amount, after the owner funds C via fallback and calls withdrawAll, the contract's entire balance is sent out so address(c).balance is 0; the mutant withdraws only 0 and leaves a nonzero balance.

For any owner and any funded balance, calling withdrawAll() transfers the entire contract balance out, leaving address(c).balance == 0; the mutant never transfers, so its balance stays positive for some funded amount.

For any codeless caller, after funding c and calling withdrawAll(), the contract's entire balance is transferred out so address(c).balance becomes 0; the mutant performs no transfer and keeps a positive balance.

For any actor, withdrawAll succeeds only when the actor is the owner (the onlyOwner guard), so a non-owner's withdrawAll always reverts and leaves the balance intact; the mutant lets any non-owner drain the whole balance.
For any caller who is not the owner, a call to withdrawAll must never reduce the contract's balance (the call reverts and funds stay); the mutant lets any non-owner drain the entire balance to zero.
For any caller, a successful withdrawAll must imply the caller is the owner (non-owners always revert); the mutant lets arbitrary non-owner callers successfully withdraw the entire balance.
For any caller other than the owner, a call to withdrawAll must revert and leave the contract's balance untouched; the mutant lets an arbitrary non-owner drain the entire balance.

For any caller, withdrawAll must succeed only when the caller is the contract owner (any non-owner's call reverts and leaves funds intact); the mutant removes the onlyOwner guard so a fuzzed non-owner caller successfully drains the entire balance, breaking the rule.

For any amount v (0 <= v <= contract balance), calling withdraw(v) as the owner transfers exactly v wei out, so the contract balance afterwards equals balance - v (withdrawAll leaves 0); the mutant transfers only 1 wei instead, leaving a nonzero balance for any v > 1.

For any amount v (2 <= v <= contract balance), calling withdraw(v) as owner sends exactly v wei to the caller, increasing the caller's balance by v; the mutant sends only 1 wei, so the caller's balance increases by 1 for any v > 1.

For any admissible withdrawal amount, after funding c and having the owner call withdraw(amount), the caller's balance increases by exactly amount (funds are actually sent); the mutant sends nothing so the balance stays unchanged.

After funding c with any fuzzed amount and the owner calling withdrawAll(), c must retain zero balance because withdraw actually transfers out the funds; the mutant deletes the transfer so the balance remains unchanged.

For any amount, c.withdraw(amount) succeeds exactly when amount does not exceed c's balance (P's transfer reverts otherwise), while the mutant's empty withdraw always succeeds, breaking the rule for amounts above the balance.

For any admissible owner, funding, and amount not exceeding c's balance, calling c.withdraw(amount) must reduce address(c).balance by exactly amount; the mutant deletes the transfer so the balance never changes.

For any admissible amount, once the owner withdraws the entire balance via withdraw, a subsequent withdrawal attempt must revert because the funds have actually left the contract; the mutant never sends funds, so its follow-up withdrawal still succeeds.
